# Classical Multidimensional Scaling of Major U.S. Airports: Geographic Reconstruction and Operational Similarity

**MAT 167 Final Project**  
**Option 26: Classical Multidimensional Scaling**

```{r}

# Experiment 1: Geographic reconstruction of U.S. airports

airports <- data.frame(
  code = c(
    "BOS", "JFK", "ATL", "MIA", "ORD",
    "DFW", "DEN", "LAX", "SFO", "SEA"
  ),

  airport = c(
    "Boston Logan International Airport",
    "John F. Kennedy International Airport",
    "Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport",
    "Miami International Airport",
    "Chicago O'Hare International Airport",
    "Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport",
    "Denver International Airport",
    "Los Angeles International Airport",
    "San Francisco International Airport",
    "Seattle-Tacoma International Airport"
  ),

  latitude = c(
    42.362944,
    40.639928,
    33.636700,
    25.795361,
    41.976940,
    32.897233,
    39.861667,
    33.942496,
    37.618806,
    47.449889
  ),

  longitude = c(
    -71.006389,
    -73.778692,
    -84.427864,
    -80.290116,
    -87.908150,
    -97.037695,
    -104.673167,
    -118.408049,
    -122.375417,
    -122.311778
  )
)

# Display the data
print(airports)
```


```{r}
# Convert to planar coordinates

# Earth's approximate radius in kilometers
earth_radius <- 6371

# Convert degrees to radians
lat_rad <- airports$latitude * pi / 180
lon_rad <- airports$longitude * pi / 180

# Use the average airport location as the center
center_lat <- mean(lat_rad)
center_lon <- mean(lon_rad)

# Approximate planar coordinates in kilometers
airports$x_km <- earth_radius *
  cos(center_lat) *
  (lon_rad - center_lon)

airports$y_km <- earth_radius *
  (lat_rad - center_lat)

# Display the new coordinates
print(airports[, c("code", "x_km", "y_km")])
```

```{r}
# Draw a map showing the original airport location
plot(
  airports$x_km,
  airports$y_km,
  type = "n",
  asp = 1,
  xlim = range(airports$x_km) + c(-300, 300),
  ylim = range(airports$y_km) + c(-250, 250),
  xlab = "East-West Position (km)",
  ylab = "North-South Position (km)",
  main = "Original Geographic Configuration of 10 U.S. Airports")

points(
  airports$x_km,
  airports$y_km,
  pch = 19,
  cex = 1.2
)

text(
  airports$x_km,
  airports$y_km,
  labels = airports$code,
  pos = 3,
  cex = 0.9
)
```

```{r}
# Calculate the distance matrix

# Create the coordinate matrix
X_original <- as.matrix(
  airports[, c("x_km", "y_km")]
)

rownames(X_original) <- airports$code

# Compute pairwise Euclidean distances
airport_dist <- dist(
  X_original,
  method = "euclidean"
)

# Convert the dist object into a full matrix
D <- as.matrix(airport_dist)

# Display the distance matrix
round(D, 1)
```

```{r}
round(D, 1)

D["BOS", "JFK"]
D["BOS", "SFO"]
D["LAX", "SFO"]

isSymmetric(D)
diag(D)
```

```{r}
# Square every entry in the distance matrix
D_squared <- D^2

round(D_squared, 0)
```

```{r}
# Construct the centering matrix

# Number of airports
n <- nrow(D)

# Centering matrix
J <- diag(n) - matrix(1 / n, nrow = n, ncol = n)

round(J, 2)
```

```{r}
# Double centering

# Recover the Gram matrix using double centering
B <- -0.5 * J %*% D_squared %*% J

rownames(B) <- airports$code
colnames(B) <- airports$code

round(B, 1)
```

```{r}
# check
isSymmetric(B)

round(rowSums(B), 8)
```

```{r}
# Gram matrix calculated directly from the original coordinates
B_original <- X_original %*% t(X_original)

# Compare the two Gram matrices
max(abs(B - B_original))
```

```{r}
# Eigendecomposition of the Gram matrix
eig_B <- eigen(B, symmetric = TRUE)

# Eigenvalues
eig_values <- eig_B$values

# Eigenvectors
eig_vectors <- eig_B$vectors

round(eig_values, 6)
```

```{r}
# Keep the two largest eigenvalues
lambda_2 <- diag(eig_values[1:2])

# Keep the corresponding eigenvectors
V_2 <- eig_vectors[, 1:2]

# Reconstruct two-dimensional coordinates
X_mds <- V_2 %*% sqrt(lambda_2)

rownames(X_mds) <- airports$code
colnames(X_mds) <- c("MDS1", "MDS2")

round(X_mds, 2)
```

```{r}
# Distances from the reconstructed coordinates
D_mds <- as.matrix(dist(X_mds))

# Maximum difference between original and reconstructed distances
max(abs(D - D_mds))
```

```{r}
# MDS plot
plot(
  X_mds[, 1],
  X_mds[, 2],
  type = "n",
  asp = 1,
  xlim = range(X_mds[, 1]) + c(-300, 300),
  ylim = range(X_mds[, 2]) + c(-250, 250),
  xlab = "MDS Dimension 1",
  ylab = "MDS Dimension 2",
  main = "Airport Locations Reconstructed by Classical MDS"
)

points(
  X_mds[, 1],
  X_mds[, 2],
  pch = 19,
  cex = 1.2
)

text(
  X_mds[, 1],
  X_mds[, 2],
  labels = airports$code,
  pos = 3,
  cex = 0.9
)
```

```{r}
# eigenvalue plot
plot(
  1:length(eig_values),
  eig_values,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Dimension",
  ylab = "Eigenvalue",
  main = "Eigenvalues of the Gram Matrix"
)

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

```{r}
# Calculate the proportion of each of the two dimensions

# proportion of positive eigenvalues
positive_values <- eig_values[eig_values > 1e-8]

eig_proportion <- positive_values / sum(positive_values)

round(eig_proportion, 4)
round(sum(eig_proportion[1:2]), 4)
```



```{r}
# Experiment 2: Analysis of Airport Operational Similarities

# read data
airport_ops <- read.csv("airport_operations_2024.csv")

airport_ops
```

```{r}
# Create a numerical matrix

# numeric variables
ops_data <- airport_ops[, c(
  "passengers",
  "departures",
  "delay_rate",
  "cancellation_rate"
)]

rownames(ops_data) <- airport_ops$code

ops_data
```

```{r}
# standardize
ops_scaled <- scale(ops_data)

round(ops_scaled, 2)
```

```{r}
# Develop an operational differentiation matrix
# check the standarize
round(colMeans(ops_scaled), 10)

round(apply(ops_scaled, 2, sd), 10)
```

```{r}
# operational distance matrix
D_ops <- as.matrix(dist(ops_scaled))

round(D_ops, 2)
```

```{r}
# Find the most similar and most different airport combinations

# remove diagonal (because the min is itself = 0)
D_check <- D_ops
diag(D_check) <- NA

# similar pair
which(
  D_check == min(D_check, na.rm = TRUE),
  arr.ind = TRUE
)

min(D_check, na.rm = TRUE)

# dissimilar pair
which(
  D_check == max(D_check, na.rm = TRUE),
  arr.ind = TRUE
)

max(D_check, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Perform MDS on operational distances

# double centering
n_ops <- nrow(D_ops)
J_ops <- diag(n_ops) - matrix(1 / n_ops, n_ops, n_ops)

B_ops <- -0.5 * J_ops %*% (D_ops^2) %*% J_ops

# eigendecomposition
eig_ops <- eigen(B_ops, symmetric = TRUE)

ops_values <- eig_ops$values
ops_vectors <- eig_ops$vectors

round(ops_values, 6)
```

```{r}
# Keep the first two dimensions

# two dimensions
V_ops2 <- ops_vectors[, 1:2]
L_ops2 <- diag(ops_values[1:2])

X_ops_mds <- V_ops2 %*% sqrt(L_ops2)

rownames(X_ops_mds) <- airport_ops$code
colnames(X_ops_mds) <- c("MDS1", "MDS2")

round(X_ops_mds, 2)
```

```{r}
# Examine how much information is retained by the first two dimensions

# proportion
positive_ops <- ops_values[ops_values > 1e-8]

ops_prop <- positive_ops / sum(positive_ops)

round(ops_prop, 4)
round(sum(ops_prop[1:2]), 4)
```

```{r}
# Plot the operational MDS diagram.
plot(
  X_ops_mds[, 1],
  X_ops_mds[, 2],
  type = "n",
  asp = 1,
  xlim = range(X_ops_mds[, 1]) + c(-0.5, 0.5),
  ylim = range(X_ops_mds[, 2]) + c(-0.5, 0.5),
  xlab = "MDS Dimension 1 (54.0%)",
  ylab = "MDS Dimension 2 (36.3%)",
  main = "Operational Similarity of 10 U.S. Airports"
)

points(X_ops_mds[, 1], X_ops_mds[, 2], pch = 19)

label_pos <- c(
  BOS = 1, JFK = 3, ATL = 3, MIA = 3, ORD = 2,
  DFW = 3, DEN = 3, LAX = 3, SFO = 2, SEA = 1
)

text(
  X_ops_mds[, 1],
  X_ops_mds[, 2],
  labels = rownames(X_ops_mds),
  pos = label_pos[rownames(X_ops_mds)],
  cex = 0.9
)

abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2)
```

```{r}
# dimension proportions
barplot(
  ops_prop,
  names.arg = 1:length(ops_prop),
  xlab = "MDS Dimension",
  ylab = "Proportion",
  main = "Information Retained by Each MDS Dimension"
)

abline(h = 0)
```

```{r}
# correlations with MDS dimensions
dim_cor <- cor(
  ops_scaled,
  X_ops_mds
)

round(dim_cor, 2)
```
